---
title: "CSIL design and pilot"
subtitle: "What public sources say about CSIL’s early years — without picking one start year"
---

::: {.callout-note}
## What this page covers
The exact start date of CSIL is not completely clear. Later official records describe a pilot in 1994 and province-wide availability in 1995. Another later source uses 1993. A 1995 newspaper still described CSIL as a new pilot program.

Original 1993–95 Ministry of Health records remain [wanted](../sources/wanted-ministry-csil-pilot-records.qmd). This chapter does **not** choose a single founding year.
:::

## How we use evidence

A 1995 newspaper is not the same kind of source as a 2012 official report or a later training deck. Different verbs — established, pilot, introduced, province-wide, new — are kept as the sources wrote them. Later “established” wording is not treated as a 1990s authorization.

## Why the start year is still unsettled

Later official wording gives **1994** and **1995** different meanings: pilot or introduced, then province-wide. A late-1995 source from the time still calls CSIL **new/pilot**. It does not confirm that a province-wide rollout was finished.

**1993** appears only as a later “established” label. It conflicts with the same speaker’s later “1994.” The 2008 program review dates CSIL only to “the 1990's.”

This is not a settled three-stage founding story. It is the strongest pattern the public sources now support.

## What a 1995 newspaper said

The only description from the time in this catalogue is the [HEU *Guardian*, November/December 1995](../sources/1995-heu-guardian-novdec.qmd). HEU is the Hospital Employees’ Union. The CSIL passage is on page 9.

It calls CSIL “a new program of the Community Support Branch of the Continuing Care Division” and “a pilot program.” It says non-profit societies could receive direct funding to hire caregivers. It names Sally Hamilton as the person who “manages the program for the ministry.” It says 130 people accessed CSIL funds among 65,000 continuing-care clients.

That source does not date the start to 1993, 1994, or 1995. It does not name ECPM, Creekview, Paul Gauthier, or a design committee. “Designed as a pilot” in late 1995 can mean still piloting, recently piloted, or loosely “new.” HEU had an interest in unionized home-support wages. Treat its “pilot” wording as HEU’s report, not as a ministry file.

## What a later official report said

[Ombudsperson, *The Best of Care* Part 2 (2012)](../sources/2012-ombudsperson-best-of-care.qmd) is a later official account. It is not a 1990s file.

It says CSIL was “established as a pilot in 1994 and implemented province-wide in 1995.” It also says the new policy required regional health boards to fund self-managed home support for people who could direct their care **or** who had a **client support group**. Elsewhere the same volume says CSIL was “introduced in 1994.”

That report does not quote the 1994 or 1995 documents. It does not name Gauthier, ECPM, Creekview, or Community Support Branch.

The 1995 “new/pilot” wording and the 2012 “province-wide in 1995” wording are **both kept**. They are not automatically the same event.

## Later “established” labels: 1993 and 1994

[Gauthier 2014](../sources/2014-gauthier-sci-csil-presentation.qmd) says CSIL was “established” in **1993**. The same deck says “The Pilot — 50 people tried it out.” [Gauthier 2015](../sources/2015-gauthier-csil-module-1.qmd) uses almost the same sentence with **1994**. [IFRC Our Team](../sources/ifrc-our-team.qmd) says Gauthier “started on the CSIL program in **1994**.”

Those are later recollections. **1993** is not in the 1995 HEU piece or the 2012 official chronology. This archive does **not** treat 1993 as a verified separate stage.

**1994** is used both as later official “pilot / introduced” and as later recollection “established” / “started.” Those verbs are not synonyms here.

The [2008 CSIL Program Review](../sources/2008-program-review-synthesis.qmd) dates CSIL to “the 1990's.” It must not be used to pick a start year.

A digest of *Hutchinson* ([2005 CanLIIDocs 513](../sources/2005-human-rights-digest-hutchinson.qmd)) says a client was accepted on CSIL in **1998**. That shows CSIL existed by 1998. It is not a founding date.

## What is still missing

No original 1993–95 Ministry of Health design file has been read. See the [wanted ministry record](../sources/wanted-ministry-csil-pilot-records.qmd).

Without those files we do not know which 1994 document the Ombudsperson treated as the “pilot.” We do not know what 1995 act counted as “province-wide.” We do not know whether “50 people tried it out” is from the time or later memory.

A 1995 Ministry of **Social Services** brokerage pilot (Kelly MacKinnon) can be confused with CSIL. It is a different program.

## Who appears in the design and pilot period

HEU 1995 names Community Support Branch / Continuing Care Division, and Sally Hamilton as program manager. The 2012 report later says regional health boards had to fund self-managed home support.

A later honour calls [Paul Gauthier](../people/paul-gauthier.qmd) “Initiator” of CSIL ([Order of Canada citation](../sources/2023-order-of-canada-paul-gauthier.qmd)). Later decks use founder language and a 50-person pilot. That is not a 1990s ministry appointment. It is not sole-founder proof.

Later IFRC wording says [Joseph Theriault](../people/joseph-theriault.qmd) travelled with Gauthier to “create and promote” CSIL. No 1990s ministry title has been found.

Gauthier 2014 later lists home-support agencies, ministry senior staff, and “consumers” as initially involved. It does not name a committee.

No 1993–95 source in this catalogue names Creekview residents, [Walt Lawrence](../people/walt-lawrence.qmd), or [Doug Mowat](../people/doug-mowat.qmd) in CSIL design. Design-group membership is **not** inferred.

Later accounts name ECPM as a pre-CSIL step. See the [ECPM chapter](ecpm.qmd). No document from the time that we have read proves official succession.

## What we still do not know

- What each of 1993, 1994, and 1995 authorized, if they authorized different things.
- How HEU’s “non-profit societies” relate to later client-support-group language (see [Later evolution](evolution.qmd)).
- Whether 1993–95 Hansard names CSIL.
- Whether a 50-person pilot is documented outside later Gauthier slides.
- Who sat on any design or advisory group, and in which year.

Those questions are not resolved by picking a start year.
